_doc: CDD guard lexicon — the repository-verification vocabulary the CDD guards assert on: the G2 cursor binary-name live-face residue ban (guards.residue — the scan token + the data-source release set), the escape-directive zero-hit (guards.escape), the whole-repo source-plane prebuilt-module zero-hit (guards.zeroDebt), the review buildability dual-evidence wording (guards.buildability), and the engine-shape restate ban the wording guard asserts on the orchestrator skills (guards.wording). Reads as the ContractLexiconGuard's guards-family data source (scripts/lib/contract-lexicon.ts); the engine command-contract vocabulary (the command and schema families) lives in the engine word table (packages/cdd-engine/config/contract-lexicon.json) and is not duplicated here. Machine-token leaves are arrays (tokens / dataSources); wording leaves are plain strings.

residue.wording: the G2 cursor binary-name live-face ban — the scan token settles to zero on the live faces except the data-source data rows that carry it (the data-row release is the sole allowed live coordinate)

escape.wording: the escape-directive ban — the two TypeScript escape directives settle to zero across the zero-debt source faces (engine src · scripts · kairos tests · the config planes) and stay fully banned: any re-appearance fails the guard; the docs face is covered by the live-face grep gate

zeroDebt.wording: the zero-debt source plane — the repository source faces carry zero prebuilt-module files: the plane is fully typed (.ts), the product build emits under dist/ (excluded from the zero-debt faces), and the orchestrator skills keep zero literal restates of the zero-debt vocabulary

buildability.evidenceWording: Buildability dual-evidence — the reviewer explicitly runs the repository's typecheck command (tsc --noEmit, or the repo equivalent) AND its test command; a buildability finding asserts both commands ran (dual evidence, not a single check)
buildability.wording: the review buildability axis — findings carry dual-evidence self-reports (typecheck + test both executed); the wording renders command descriptions, never a toolchain literal

wording.wording: the engine-shape restate ban — the orchestrator skills keep zero literal restates of the old stdout special-shape names; the modern contract referents (output contract · handoff · findings · standalone counters) are not in the set
